question: Should OpenClaw accept read-scoped runtime-config drift path names and per-cache-hit disk snapshot reads as the health diagnostic tradeoff for this PR?
rationale: The patch is additive and well-proven, but tests cannot decide whether auth/provider/secrets-adjacent path names belong on the `operator.read` health surface or whether the freshness benefit is worth synchronous disk IO on cache-hit responses.

options.title: Accept Diagnostic Boundary
options.body: Land after exact-head CI because fingerprints and detailed disk errors are admin-gated and the normal read-scoped health path proof is strong.

options.title: Request Extra Boundary Proof
options.body: Ask for a read-vs-admin transcript or a health latency sample before merge if maintainers are not comfortable with drift path visibility or disk-read cost.

options.title: Pause For Companion Policy Review
options.body: Hold this PR only if maintainers want diagnostics and the hot-mode restart-policy change in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/89517 reviewed as one product decision.

recommendation.title: Accept Diagnostic Boundary
recommendation.body: Land after exact-head CI because fingerprints and detailed disk errors are admin-gated and the normal read-scoped health path proof is strong.

likelyOwner.reason: The current checkout blame points to Vincent on the central health cache and summary construction, and this decision is about that health surface boundary.
